fatal_errors: The proposed NbTiZrHfW–Ni system is unrelated to the target HfZrTi(TaNbV)x alloy series.
The intervention of 1–2 at% Ni microalloying does not reconstruct the 1:1:1 Ta-Nb-V additions used to stabilize BCC structure.
The claimed Ni-enriched ductile phases and their mechanism are speculative and supported by no cited evidence.
Charpy impact-energy absorption is not a measurement of impact-induced chemical energy release; the target phenomenon is oxidation-driven light and sparks during high-rate fragmentation in air.
The experiment omits the approximately 4000 s^-1 SHPB loading, oxygen-containing atmosphere, high-speed imaging, and luminous-intensity analysis needed to assess energetic response.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad design objective—improving ductility while retaining strength and energetic behavior—and proposes a controlled comparison with an explicit falsification rule. However, it replaces every target-specific element: alloy composition, intervention, processing, phase evolution, mechanism, baseline, and dynamic test conditions. It provides no prior evidence that dilute Ni will form beneficial ductile regions rather than intermetallics or otherwise reduce strength. Most importantly, its proposed Charpy-type measurement conflates mechanical energy absorption with oxidation-based energy release. Thus it is a novel but presently unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction of the reported Ta-Nb-V/BCC-stabilization hypothesis.
